items.title: Building AI That Can Reason Under Uncertainty
items.creator: TWIML AI Podcast
items.description: Thore Graepel on an AlphaGo-inspired approach to reasoning, with explicit representations of knowledge and uncertainty.
items.why_recommended: A fresh episode on what reliable reasoning might need beyond a bigger language model.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: One argument for tracking uncertainty explicitly, which you can weigh against how current models reason.

items.title: The paradox at the heart of AI and science | Terence Tao
items.creator: Big Think Clips
items.description: Terence Tao on a paradox he sees where AI meets science.
items.why_recommended: Far more views than the channel's size would predict, from a mathematician known for careful judgement.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A working mathematician's view of what AI helps with in research and where care is still needed.

items.title: Why Momentum Really Works
items.creator: Gabriel Goh, Distill
items.description: An interactive article that takes momentum apart on simple quadratic problems, with sliders for step size and momentum.
items.why_recommended: You use momentum often. This shows why it speeds things up, past the usual ball-rolling story.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: See how each eigendirection converges at its own rate, and how step size and momentum trade off.

items.title: The Gleaners and I (2000)
items.creator: Agnès Varda
items.topic: gleaning and what gets thrown away
items.description: Varda's documentary about people who gather what others leave behind, and about her own way of collecting images.
items.why_recommended: A warm, playful documentary for a free evening, far from screens full of AI news.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A new way to notice waste and thrift, and how a filmmaker can put herself in the story.

items.title: Introduction to the cyanotype process
items.creator: Science and Media Museum
items.description: How to coat paper, expose it to UV light and develop a blue print in water, with some history from 1841.
items.why_recommended: A hands-on weekend option that joins chemistry, botany and photography.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Make a blue print of a leaf. Never add hydrochloric or sulphuric acid, which can release toxic gas.

cross_domain.connection: Light changes iron salts into a blue pigment. Anna Atkins used this to picture plants in her botany books.

items.title: Plausible Deniability: Getting People to Tell the Truth
items.creator: Game Changer, with Sylvain Chassang
items.description: Why anonymity is sometimes not enough to get honest reports, and how plausible deniability can help, with field work in garment factories.
items.why_recommended: A short episode where economics meets a question that also sits under privacy research.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: How to design a reporting system so that telling the truth is safer for the person who speaks.

cross_domain.connection: Adding deniability to answers is also the idea behind randomized response, a root of differential privacy.

items.title: Why the Soviet GitHub Failed
items.creator: Asianometry
items.description: A history of a Soviet effort to share software, and why it did not work.
items.why_recommended: It drew unusually active discussion for the channel's size, on a story rarely told.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A concrete case of why sharing code needs more than a central place to put it.

items.title: Scientists Said This Wave Was Impossible
items.creator: Veritasium
items.description: Do monster waves really exist? A look at rogue waves and the physics of waves adding up.
items.why_recommended: A well-watched new explainer that turns a sailors' story into a physics question.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: An idea of how waves can combine into one far larger than those around it.

items.title: Taking turns isn't fair. We fixed it.
items.creator: Stand-up Maths
items.description: Matt Parker on why simple alternation can favour one side, and what orders such as ABBA BAAB do about it.
items.why_recommended: Very strong likes and comments for the channel. Light, funny and useful in daily life.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A fairer way to order turns the next time two people pick, serve or share.

items.title: The Evolution of Trust
items.creator: Nicky Case
items.description: A playable explanation of repeated trust games.
items.why_recommended: Play it after the deniability episode. It lets you test when cooperation survives.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A feel for how repeated meetings and honest mistakes change which strategy wins.

items.title: Elements of Meaningful Conversation: Fewer Mirror Questions, More Follow-Ups
items.creator: Alison Wood Brooks, HBS Working Knowledge
items.description: A book excerpt on four kinds of questions, drawing on a study of get-to-know-you conversations between strangers.
items.why_recommended: A short, practical read on listening that you can try in your next conversation.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: Why follow-up questions raise liking, while bouncing a question back does much less.

items.title: Tabula Rasa
items.creator: Arvo Pärt, ECM
items.description: The ECM album of Pärt's music with Gidon Kremer, Keith Jarrett and others. Start with Fratres.
items.why_recommended: A landmark recording and a quiet change of pace at the end of the week.
items.what_i_might_get_from_it: A sense of how very few notes and patient repetition can carry deep feeling.

notes: Podcasts and videos come from the candidate files fetched on 26 November.
